title: India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) Enters into Force
summary: The India-UK Free Trade Agreement, officially termed the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), came into force on July 15, 2026. Under the deal, nearly 99% of Indian exports gain duty-free access to the UK market, covering textiles, leather goods, footwear, and engineering products. The UK will see reduced tariffs on Scotch whisky, automobiles, and luxury goods entering India. The first consignments valued at USD 4,46,046 were flagged off from Chennai, and the UK Trade Minister described it as the 'fastest implementation' of any trade deal.
exam_angle: This is a landmark bilateral trade agreement with direct implications for India's exports, FDI, and services sector. Aspirants must know the key sectors benefited, the investment-pact component, and the broader India-UK strategic relationship.
key_facts: Agreement: India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Effective date: July 15, 2026
Nearly 99% of Indian exports to get duty-free access to UK
First consignment flagged off from Chennai worth USD 4,46,046

title: 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill (Delimitation): Political Manoeuvring Ahead of Parliament
summary: The 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill on delimitation has become a major political flashpoint, with the BJP reportedly wooing NCP (SP) and DMK for support. NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule stated her party would back the delimitation bill with certain riders but ruled out joining the NDA. Senior Congress leader P. Chidambaram alleged the BJP is wooing regional parties to secure the two-thirds majority needed for a constitutional amendment. The bill seeks to redraw parliamentary and assembly constituencies based on the 2021 census data.
exam_angle: Delimitation is governed by Articles 82 and 170 of the Constitution; a constitutional amendment bill requires a special majority under Article 368. This item connects to federalism, representation, and scheduled constitutional bodies like the Delimitation Commission.
key_facts: Bill: 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill (Delimitation)
Requires special majority under Article 368 of the Constitution
Key parties being wooed: NCP (SP), DMK
Delimitation governed by Articles 82 (Lok Sabha) and 170 (State Assemblies)

title: US Senate Bill Proposes 100% Tariff on Countries Buying Russian Oil; India Faces Risk
summary: US Senators unveiled a bill proposing 100% secondary tariffs on India, China, and three other countries that continue purchasing Russian crude oil, revised downward from an earlier threatened 500% tariff. President Trump backed the legislation as part of broader sanctions pressure on Russia amid the ongoing Ukraine conflict. India, which has been the largest buyer of discounted Russian oil since 2022, faces significant economic risk if the bill is enacted. The development adds fresh uncertainty to India's energy security and import diversification strategy.
exam_angle: This directly impacts India's energy security, crude oil import policy, and India-US relations. It also connects to the broader debate on secondary sanctions, CAATSA, and India's strategic autonomy.
key_facts: Proposed tariff: 100% on countries buying Russian oil (revised from 500%)
Countries targeted: India, China, and three others
India has been Russia's largest oil buyer post-2022 Ukraine war
Bill backed by US President Trump as part of Russia sanctions package

title: Indian Sailor Killed in Strait of Hormuz Attack; India Summons Iranian Ambassador
summary: An Indian seafarer was killed when his vessel was struck during US-Iran hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz, making it one of the first Indian casualties in the conflict. India's Ministry of External Affairs summoned the Iranian Ambassador to lodge a strong protest, condemning attacks on vessels carrying Indian crew. The Indian government also announced it would account for every Indian seafarer irrespective of the flag of the vessel. The Strait of Hormuz handles approximately 20% of global oil trade and its closure threatens global energy supplies.
exam_angle: The Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for global oil trade; India's response—summoning an envoy—is an important diplomatic tool. This connects to GS Paper 2 (IR) themes of diaspora welfare, maritime security, and India's West Asia policy.
key_facts: An Indian sailor was killed in a strike on a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz
India summoned the Iranian Ambassador in protest
Government pledged to track all Indian seafarers regardless of vessel flag
Strait of Hormuz handles ~20% of global oil trade

title: US-Iran Military Conflict: Hormuz Blockade Reimposed, Strikes on Iranian Facilities
summary: The United States reimposed a naval blockade on Iran and launched fresh strikes on Iranian military facilities, including what reports described as an Iranian Army base, killing at least seven. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed counter-strikes on US military sites in the Gulf. Iran threatened to block additional vital seaways and declared Hormuz would remain closed until the US ceased its military operations. Trump warned of further strikes on Iranian power plants and bridges if no deal was reached.
exam_angle: The US-Iran conflict and Hormuz closure directly affects India's oil imports, diaspora safety, and regional stability in West Asia—a recurring theme in GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Energy Security).
key_facts: US reimposed Hormuz naval blockade against Iran
US strikes reportedly killed at least 7 at Iranian Army base
IRGC claimed counter-strikes on US military sites in the Gulf
Iran threatened to block additional seaways

title: Iran Used Mobile Data Roaming and Ad-Tech to Track US Military Personnel in Gulf
summary: A Financial Times investigation revealed that Iran used commercial mobile data roaming networks and advertising technology (ad-tech) to covertly track the movements of US military personnel across the Middle East. The technique involved exploiting data from mobile networks and digital advertising ecosystems to triangulate locations of servicemen. This represents a significant non-kinetic intelligence and cyber-surveillance capability used in an active conflict zone. The revelation has raised alarms about the vulnerability of commercial digital infrastructure to state-level exploitation.
exam_angle: This is relevant to GS Paper 3 (Internal Security/Cyber Security) themes of cyber warfare, information warfare, and the dual-use nature of commercial technology in modern conflicts.
key_facts: Iran exploited mobile data roaming and ad-tech platforms to track US troops
Technique used commercial digital infrastructure for state-level surveillance
Reported by the Financial Times
Highlights vulnerability of commercial networks to military intelligence exploitation

title: PM Modi Claimed to Have Helped Prevent Russia's Tactical Nuclear Strike on Ukraine in 2022: Polish Minister
summary: A Polish minister claimed that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi played a role in dissuading Russian President Vladimir Putin from launching a tactical nuclear strike on Ukraine in 2022. The claim, reported by The Times of India, suggests back-channel diplomatic engagement by India during a critical phase of the Russia-Ukraine war. India had publicly stated in September 2022 that 'this is not an era of war' during Modi's meeting with Putin in Samarkand. India's strategic autonomy and its unique position as a mediator between Russia and the West are highlighted by this claim.
exam_angle: India's strategic autonomy, its relationship with Russia, and its role as a peace mediator are key IR themes. The Samarkand statement connects to PM Modi's diplomacy and India's stated opposition to nuclear use.
key_facts: Claim made by a Polish minister regarding 2022 Russia-Ukraine war
Modi reportedly persuaded Putin against using tactical nuclear weapons
Modi's Samarkand statement (Sept 2022): 'This is not an era of war'
Highlights India's strategic autonomy and mediatory role

title: Air India Crash Probe: AAIB Tells Supreme Court Draft Report Due by October 2026
summary: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) informed the Supreme Court of India that the draft final report on the June 2025 Air India crash will be ready by October 2026. The AAIB also told the court that cockpit voice recordings cannot be shared publicly during the ongoing investigation. The Supreme Court is monitoring the probe after concerns were raised that a 'pilot-blame narrative' was potentially influencing witnesses. The crash, which occurred in June 2025, is one of India's deadliest aviation disasters.
exam_angle: This connects to the role of statutory investigation bodies (AAIB under the Aircraft Act), the Supreme Court's suo motu jurisdiction, and the importance of impartial accident investigations in civil aviation governance.
key_facts: Investigating body: Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB)
Draft final report expected: October 2026
Cockpit voice recordings ruled non-shareable during investigation
Supreme Court monitoring probe amid concerns over witness influence

title: Supreme Court Questions Whether English Can Be Considered an Indigenous Indian Language
summary: The Supreme Court of India raised an intriguing constitutional and socio-linguistic question, asking whether English can be considered an indigenous Indian language given its deep entrenchment in public life, judiciary, and administration over centuries. The observation was made during proceedings likely related to a language-policy or medium-of-instruction case. The remark has significant implications for debates around the three-language formula, the Official Languages Act, and the constitutional status of English under the Eighth Schedule. English is not listed in the Eighth Schedule but continues as an associate official language under Article 343.
exam_angle: Constitutional provisions on language policy (Articles 343–351), the Eighth Schedule, and debates around linguistic identity and the three-language formula are directly relevant for GS Paper 2.
key_facts: Supreme Court questioned if English qualifies as an indigenous Indian language
English is NOT listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution
English continues as associate official language under Article 343(2)
Eighth Schedule currently lists 22 scheduled languages

title: India Bans Import of Goods Manufactured Using Forced Labour
summary: India has announced a ban on the import of goods manufactured using forced labour, even as a US investigation into the matter remains pending. The move aligns India with global trade norms around ethical supply chains and may be partly aimed at preempting US trade scrutiny. The ban was announced by the Ministry of Commerce and connects to provisions under WTO agreements on trade and human rights. The policy is significant in the context of India's positioning as an alternative manufacturing hub and its sensitivity around supply chain due diligence.
exam_angle: This policy connects to GS Paper 3 themes of trade policy, ethical supply chains, and India's WTO obligations. It also reflects India's proactive trade diplomacy especially in the context of US scrutiny.
key_facts: India bans imports of goods made using forced labour
Announced by the Ministry of Commerce
Move aligns with US and EU ethical trade requirements
Relevant to WTO rules on trade and labour standards

title: National Health Research Policy 2026 Released: India to Overhaul Public Health Research System
summary: The Indian government released the National Health Research Policy 2026, aimed at overhauling the country's health research system to better align it with public health priorities. The policy seeks to strengthen translational research, bridge gaps between laboratory findings and clinical applications, and increase domestic funding for health R&D. It envisages greater coordination between the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), academic institutions, and industry. The policy is being seen as a strategic response to lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic.
exam_angle: National health policies and ICMR's role are frequently tested in GS Paper 2 (Health/Governance). The policy's emphasis on translational research and public health linkages is a key exam takeaway.
key_facts: Policy: National Health Research Policy 2026
Released by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Key body: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)
Focus: Translational research, public health alignment, post-COVID lessons

title: IDBI Bank Stake Sale Process Revived; Government Keen to Expedite Disinvestment
summary: The Union government has signalled renewed intent to proceed with the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank, with reports indicating the process has been placed back on the priority list. The government and Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) together hold a majority stake in IDBI Bank, and the disinvestment has been pending since 2021 when it was first announced. The Reserve Bank of India's 'fit and proper' criteria for the new owner remain a key hurdle. The move is part of the government's broader disinvestment and asset monetisation strategy.
exam_angle: IDBI Bank disinvestment is a longstanding topic in GS Paper 3 (Economy) covering privatisation, PSU reforms, and the role of LIC as a state investor. Aspirants must know the shareholding structure and regulatory hurdles.
key_facts: Government + LIC together hold majority stake in IDBI Bank
Disinvestment first announced in Union Budget 2021-22
RBI 'fit and proper' criteria for buyer remains a key regulatory hurdle
Part of the government's National Monetisation Pipeline/disinvestment agenda

title: FBI Adds Indian Gangster Nitish Kaushal alias 'Lala' to Most Wanted List
summary: The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) added Indian gangster Nitish Kaushal, alias 'Lala', to its Most Wanted list. Kaushal is reportedly a key associate of Jaggu Bhagwanpuria, who is himself linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. The network is accused of extortion, murder, and transnational organised crime. India's Ministry of External Affairs reaffirmed India's commitment to combating terrorism and organised crime in the context of these arrests and listings.
exam_angle: Transnational organised crime, extradition mechanisms, and India-US law enforcement cooperation are relevant GS Paper 3 (Internal Security) topics. The Bishnoi gang's international reach is a frequently appearing current affairs theme.
key_facts: Nitish Kaushal alias 'Lala' added to FBI Most Wanted list
Associate of Jaggu Bhagwanpuria, linked to Lawrence Bishnoi gang
Network accused of extortion, murder, transnational crime
MEA reaffirmed India's commitment to fighting terror and organised crime

title: India Blames Pakistan for Protests in Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir (PoK)
summary: India formally accused Pakistan of instigating and organising protests in Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir (PoK) and demanded accountability from Islamabad. The Indian government stated that the unrest in PoK reflects the Pakistani state's use of local grievances for strategic purposes. This comes amid continuing tensions over cross-border terrorism and the status of Jammu & Kashmir following the revocation of Article 370 in 2019. India has consistently maintained that PoK is an integral part of India illegally occupied by Pakistan.
exam_angle: PoK, Article 370, India-Pakistan relations, and the Line of Control (LoC) are perennial GS Paper 2 (IR) topics. India's diplomatic positioning on PoK protests is exam-relevant.
key_facts: India accused Pakistan of fomenting protests in PoK
India maintains PoK is an integral part of India under illegal occupation
Connects to Article 370 abrogation (August 2019) and Jammu & Kashmir reorganisation
Pakistan-occupied territories include PoK and Gilgit-Baltistan

title: Jaishankar Attends India-EU Summit in Brussels; Meets European Council President
summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar attended the India-EU Summit in Brussels and met the President of the European Council, signalling advancement in India-EU strategic ties. The discussions covered trade and technology cooperation, the stalled India-EU FTA negotiations, and geopolitical coordination. Jaishankar described the India-EU relationship as having 'advanced significantly' post-summit. The India-EU Summit is a key platform for reviewing the Strategic Partnership established in 2004.
exam_angle: India-EU relations, the Strategic Partnership of 2004, and the India-EU FTA (Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement—BTIA) negotiations are important IR topics for the exam.
key_facts: EAM Jaishankar attended India-EU Summit in Brussels
Met European Council President to discuss trade and technology
India-EU Strategic Partnership established in 2004
India-EU BTIA (FTA) negotiations have been ongoing since 2007

title: QS Asia University Rankings 2026: India's Position Among Top 10 Asian Universities
summary: India Today reported on the QS Asia University Rankings 2026, examining whether any Indian institution features among Asia's top 10 universities. Historically, Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) have featured in the top tier of Asian rankings, with IIT Bombay and IIT Delhi among the highest-placed Indian institutions. The QS rankings are published by Quacquarelli Symonds and are based on academic reputation, employer reputation, faculty-to-student ratio, and research citations. India's higher education performance is benchmarked globally through such rankings under the National Education Policy 2020 goals.
exam_angle: University rankings, the National Education Policy 2020, and India's global higher education ambitions are relevant to GS Paper 2 (Education/Governance). QS, THE, and NIRF are the key ranking systems aspirants must know.
key_facts: Ranking: QS Asia University Rankings 2026 (published by Quacquarelli Symonds)
Top Indian institutions: IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi typically among highest-placed
Rankings based on: Academic reputation, employer reputation, citations, faculty ratio
India's domestic ranking system: NIRF (National Institutional Ranking Framework)

title: Dara Singh (Graham Staines Murder Convict) May Be Released on Independence Day
summary: Dara Singh, the main convict in the 1999 murder of Australian missionary Graham Staines and his two young sons in Odisha, may be released from prison around Independence Day (August 15), according to media reports. Dara Singh was sentenced to life imprisonment by the Supreme Court in 2011 after his death sentence was commuted. The Staines murder case was a landmark in debates around minority rights, communal violence, and judicial process in India. The potential release has reignited public discourse on remission of sentences in heinous crimes.
exam_angle: The Staines murder case is relevant to GS Paper 2 (Polity/Governance) topics on remission of sentences under Articles 72 and 161, minority rights, and the Supreme Court's commutation of death sentences.
key_facts: Convict: Dara Singh, main accused in 1999 Graham Staines murder case
Victim: Graham Staines and his two sons, burned alive in Keonjhar, Odisha
Supreme Court commuted death sentence to life imprisonment in 2011
Remission of sentences governed by Articles 72 (President) and 161 (Governor)
source: The Times of India / India Today

title: India-US Defence Technology Ties: Aspirations Outpace Actual Delivery
summary: An analysis in The Hindu highlighted that despite ambitious frameworks such as the Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology (iCET) and the Defence Industrial Cooperation Roadmap, actual technology transfer from the US to India remains limited. Key areas like jet engine co-production (GE F414 for Tejas Mk2), armed drones, and semiconductor supply chains are progressing slowly. The article noted structural impediments including US export control laws (ITAR/EAR), bureaucratic delays, and differences in industrial capability. India's push for 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' in defence makes this gap particularly significant.
exam_angle: India-US defence cooperation, iCET, ITAR/EAR export controls, and Aatmanirbhar Bharat in defence are key GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Defence) topics.
key_facts: Framework: Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology (iCET), launched 2023
Key project: GE F414 engine co-production for Tejas Mk2 fighter jet
US export control laws (ITAR/EAR) remain a structural barrier
India's defence self-reliance goal under Aatmanirbhar Bharat
